review.notes: Complete actual native functions, tables and views exports across all five public schemas reconcile to 90 distinct names. All overloads retained and deduplicated by schema/name. Current runtime independently captured at public main; differences from v0.3.0 are added metadata/composed examples, and named signatures agree. Notebook receipts retain the released runtime revision; exact-current analytical execution is not claimed.

Current runtime independently captured at public main; differences from v0.3.0 are added metadata/composed examples, and named signatures agree. Notebook receipts retain the released runtime revision; exact-current analytical execution is not claimed.

review.purpose: Use diversity.observed_features in the focused analytical question of notebook 01, with the returned values displayed and reconciled.
review.finding: Richness counts positive features, retaining explicit zeros in the input. A_base and B_scaled both have four observed features under uniform count scaling.

review.purpose: Use diversity.shannon in the focused analytical question of notebook 01, with the returned values displayed and reconciled.
review.finding: Natural-log entropy is independently reconstructed from worker proportions. Equal composition and rescaling preserve Shannon entropy; feature relabeling can also preserve this summary.

review.purpose: Use diversity.hill in the focused analytical question of notebook 01, with the returned values displayed and reconciled.
review.finding: Order-one Hill diversity equals exp(Shannon); SQL/presentation checks the relation and bounds it between one and observed richness. Effective-feature units differ from entropy units.

review.purpose: Use stats.closure in the focused analytical question of notebook 01, with the returned values displayed and reconciled.
review.finding: All 30 proportions are reconciled with original count divided by sample total. Closed Bray–Curtis is zero for a uniformly scaled duplicate even when raw distance is nonzero.

review.purpose: Use diversity.beta_diversity in the focused analytical question of notebook 01, with the returned values displayed and reconciled.
review.finding: Both complete six-sample Bray–Curtis matrices are reconstructed in SQL. The scaled duplicate has raw distance 1/2 at multiplier 3 and 7/9 at 8, while its proportion distance remains zero.

review.purpose: Use sequence.is_valid_dna in the focused analytical question of notebook 02, with the returned values displayed and reconciled.
review.finding: All six records stay in the audit; valid DNA can contain a gap or ambiguity symbol. Missing remains unknown and malformed input is false.

review.purpose: Use sequence.has_gaps in the focused analytical question of notebook 02, with the returned values displayed and reconciled.
review.finding: The gapped row is distinguished from ungapped valid strings before an explicit coordinate-changing gap removal.

review.purpose: Use sequence.has_degenerates in the focused analytical question of notebook 02, with the returned values displayed and reconciled.
review.finding: The N-containing row is valid but ambiguous and excluded from definite-base profiles, without inventing its missing base.

review.purpose: Use sequence.degap in the focused analytical question of notebook 02, with the returned values displayed and reconciled.
review.finding: The gapped string becomes the authored forward string and is included in the three eligible representations; the input audit retains its original form.

review.purpose: Use sequence.complement in the focused analytical question of notebook 02, with the returned values displayed and reconciled.
review.finding: The complement string is displayed beside the reverse complement to distinguish base substitution from reversing order.

review.purpose: Use sequence.reverse_complement in the focused analytical question of notebook 02, with the returned values displayed and reconciled.
review.finding: The authored reverse row is verified and k-mer reverse complements define the explicit strand-collapsed profile keys.

review.purpose: Use sequence.is_reverse_complement in the focused analytical question of notebook 02, with the returned values displayed and reconciled.
review.finding: The reverse row is identified as the reverse complement of the fixed forward input; this is a representation check, not biological identity.

review.purpose: Use sequence.transcribe in the focused analytical question of notebook 02, with the returned values displayed and reconciled.
review.finding: The RNA representation is displayed for each eligible string; T-to-U transcription is separate from strand reversal.

review.purpose: Use sequence.reverse_transcribe in the focused analytical question of notebook 02, with the returned values displayed and reconciled.
review.finding: Every displayed RNA returns to its original gapless DNA in an explicit round-trip invariant.

review.purpose: Use sequence.gc_frequency in the focused analytical question of notebook 02, with the returned values displayed and reconciled.
review.finding: Each eligible string has seven G/C bases, independently reconstructed by summing G and C residue counts.

review.purpose: Use sequence.gc_content in the focused analytical question of notebook 02, with the returned values displayed and reconciled.
review.finding: Each eligible representation has GC fraction 7/15, reconstructed from raw GC counts and complete string length.

review.purpose: Use sequence.count_subsequence in the focused analytical question of notebook 02, with the returned values displayed and reconciled.
review.finding: The literal ATG motif occurs once in forward/gapless strings and zero times in the reverse string despite equal GC. This is not gene annotation.

review.purpose: Use sequence.residue_frequencies in the focused analytical question of notebook 02, with the returned values displayed and reconciled.
review.finding: All base-count rows sum to the complete length of 15; G+C residue totals independently agree with the two GC scalar outputs.

review.purpose: Use sequence.kmer_frequencies in the focused analytical question of notebook 02, with the returned values displayed and reconciled.
review.finding: Overlapping windows reconcile with length minus k plus one. Complete pairwise shared-mass matrices retain zero overlaps and show the effect of oriented versus reverse-complement-collapsed profiles.

review.purpose: Use sequence.hamming_distance in the focused analytical question of notebook 03, with the returned values displayed and reconciled.
review.finding: One mismatch in 15 positions gives 1/15; unequal-length deletion/flank comparisons stay NULL rather than being called identical.

review.purpose: Use sequence.mismatch_count in the focused analytical question of notebook 03, with the returned values displayed and reconciled.
review.finding: Two authored substitutions each have one positional base mismatch but different translated-string equality.

review.purpose: Use sequence.match_count in the focused analytical question of notebook 03, with the returned values displayed and reconciled.
review.finding: Matches plus mismatches reconstruct the full equal-length input; unequal lengths remain unavailable.

review.purpose: Use alignment.align_score_nucleotide in the focused analytical question of notebook 03, with the returned values displayed and reconciled.
review.finding: Fixed global scalar scores agree with global alignment-table scores. Selected local mode may change span and score, without changing the scalar reference. Nucleotide defaults also change match/mismatch weights from +1/-2 to +2/-3, explicitly separating span changes from scoring-objective changes.

review.purpose: Use alignment.pairwise_align_nucleotide in the focused analytical question of notebook 03, with the returned values displayed and reconciled.
review.finding: Actual aligned strings and lengths are displayed for all five pairs. Global terminal-gap behavior and local subregion selection remain explicit.

review.purpose: Use sequence.translate in the focused analytical question of notebook 03, with the returned values displayed and reconciled.
review.finding: The stipulated standard-code frame maps synonymous and unchanged DNA to MRITK while the other one-base variant yields MRIPK; the codon deletion yields MITK.

review.purpose: Use sequence.is_valid_protein in the focused analytical question of notebook 03, with the returned values displayed and reconciled.
review.finding: Translated strings pass alphabet validation, but the displayed ACGT control also passes, while malformed and missing controls remain false/unknown. Alphabet validity does not identify molecular type.

review.purpose: Use alignment.align_score_protein in the focused analytical question of notebook 03, with the returned values displayed and reconciled.
review.finding: Protein scalar scores reconcile with global protein table scores and are kept in separate units from nucleotide scores.

review.purpose: Use alignment.pairwise_align_protein in the focused analytical question of notebook 03, with the returned values displayed and reconciled.
review.finding: The four frame-specified protein pairs retain aligned strings, selected score and aligned length. Mode changes are interpreted as comparison changes, not functional-effect predictions.

review.purpose: Use sequence.translate_six_frames in the focused analytical question of notebook 03, with the returned values displayed and reconciled.
review.finding: All six frame candidates, lengths and stop-symbol counts are displayed for the fixed reference; +1 matches the stipulated translation. Enumeration does not select a true gene.

review.purpose: Use stats.clr in the focused analytical question of notebook 04, with the returned values displayed and reconciled.
review.finding: Twelve natural-log coordinates have per-sample sum zero and match log-part minus mean log-part in SQL.

review.purpose: Use stats.ilr in the focused analytical question of notebook 04, with the returned values displayed and reconciled.
review.finding: Eight orthonormal coordinates preserve each CLR squared norm. Component indices are explicitly not feature identities.

review.purpose: Use stats.alr in the focused analytical question of notebook 04, with the returned values displayed and reconciled.
review.finding: Eight log-ratios use a visible zero-based reference derived from named feature order. Switching a to c changes only ALR coordinates and labels.

review.purpose: Use stats.clr_inv in the focused analytical question of notebook 04, with the returned values displayed and reconciled.
review.finding: All twelve recovered proportions match closure; numeric inverse part indices are mapped back to explicit a/b/c feature names.

review.purpose: Use stats.ilr_inv in the focused analytical question of notebook 04, with the returned values displayed and reconciled.
review.finding: Two coordinates per sample recover three proportions using the same default basis. All twelve parts reconcile without claiming original-count recovery.

review.purpose: Use stats.alr_inv in the focused analytical question of notebook 04, with the returned values displayed and reconciled.
review.finding: Matching the selected reference index recovers all twelve closed proportions for either reference feature; mismatched references are not silently accepted.

review.purpose: Use stats.pairwise_vlr in the focused analytical question of notebook 04, with the returned values displayed and reconciled.
review.finding: All nine feature-pair variances match SQL var_samp of log ratios. The fixed b=2a relation yields zero a/b variance while ratios with c vary; this is descriptive synthetic variation.

review.purpose: Use tree.neighbor_joining in the focused analytical question of notebook 05, with the returned values displayed and reconciled.
review.finding: Both reference and selected neighbor-joining Newick trees retain four tips. Uniform positive input scaling changes lengths while preserving the within-method topology.

review.purpose: Use tree.upgma in the focused analytical question of notebook 05, with the returned values displayed and reconciled.
review.finding: Reference and selected UPGMA trees retain four tips and the rooted ultrametric construction is distinguished from the other methods. Root-dependent height is not interpreted as age.

review.purpose: Use tree.gme in the focused analytical question of notebook 05, with the returned values displayed and reconciled.
review.finding: Greedy-minimum-evolution output participates in the same tip-count, length/height scaling and comparison audit rather than being listed as a catalog name.

review.purpose: Use tree.bme in the focused analytical question of notebook 05, with the returned values displayed and reconciled.
review.finding: Balanced-minimum-evolution output is separately materialized, displayed and measured. This small matrix tests scale behavior without inferring method superiority.

review.purpose: Use tree.tip_count in the focused analytical question of notebook 05, with the returned values displayed and reconciled.
review.finding: All eight constructed trees retain the complete four-label denominator; controlled trees also retain those four tips.

review.purpose: Use tree.total_branch_length in the focused analytical question of notebook 05, with the returned values displayed and reconciled.
review.finding: The actual stored-edge total is measured for every method and scale. The controlled scaled tree has total length 6 times the selected factor.

review.purpose: Use tree.tree_height in the focused analytical question of notebook 05, with the returned values displayed and reconciled.
review.finding: Serialized-root height is measured separately from total edge length and verified to scale within each method; different roots are not treated as comparable biological ages.

review.purpose: Use tree.robinson_foulds in the focused analytical question of notebook 05, with the returned values displayed and reconciled.
review.finding: The topology-swapped control has four differing rooted splits; identical and uniformly scaled controls have zero split distance.

review.purpose: Use tree.weighted_robinson_foulds in the focused analytical question of notebook 05, with the returned values displayed and reconciled.
review.finding: The topology swap and non-unit length scaling are detected, distinguishing branch-length changes from split changes.

review.purpose: Use tree.cophenetic_distance in the focused analytical question of notebook 05, with the returned values displayed and reconciled.
review.finding: The actual upstream default is unit correlation (1-r)/2, independent of positive common scale. The controlled scaled tree can have changed absolute lengths but zero distance; a topology swap returns 0.75.
